title: Specs flow flaked in the dev org: a spec search ran before the queued indexing job wrote the document
summary: The routine extended `echopoint: specs` to cover spec search (echopoint#508) with three search nodes that ran right after `create-spec`. Spec search documents are written by a queued sync job after the create commits, not inside it, so a search that lands before the job finds nothing. The third repeat run in the dev org did exactly that: `search-slug` saw an empty result while the two searches that ran a few milliseconds later found the spec. The flow now waits through a poll module (`specs: search poll (module)`) until the slug is searchable, then runs the searches; it passed three times in each org, and one dev run needed a retry, which shows the lag is real. The flow-suite-testing skill now says that a read of a projection polls.

impact.text: One failed authoring run of `echopoint: specs` in the dev org. The racy definition was saved to the CI-tagged flow in both orgs for about six minutes; no scheduled or CI suite run used it.

trigger: The updated `echopoint: specs` definition, with search nodes wired straight after `create-spec`, was saved to the CI org and then mirrored to the dev org.
detection: The authoring loop's third repeat run in the dev org failed on `search-slug` (`JSONPath '$.groups[0].items[*].identifiers.spec_slug' did not match any nodes`). Three CI-org runs and two dev-org runs had passed, because the job usually lands first.
resolution: A poll module searches by the run's slug every 500 ms (30 s budget) until the spec is found; `search-slug`, `search-partial-slug` and `search-title` run after it. Both orgs were updated, validated and run three times each, all green. Two first attempts at the module failed on runner mechanics (a `{{$runId}}` in a module binding, a JSONPath into a final output); those lessons are in the skill too.

whys.problem: `echopoint: specs` failed in the dev org: searching a just-created spec by its exact slug returned no spec

because.text: `search-slug` ran about 50 ms after `create-spec` answered, before the spec's search document existed
because.evidence: Run `01a110eb-e5fd`: `search-slug` empty, sibling searches a few ms later found the spec; a later dev run needed one poll retry

because.text: Spec search documents are written by a queued job (`echopoint.resource_search.sync`, 250 ms poll) after the create commits
The flow treated search as read-your-writes: the #508 commit says the document is replaced inside the write's transaction
because.evidence: [4ba6cd1d](https://github.com/nanostack-dev/echopoint/commit/4ba6cd1dce26947a84d2f774885b7837b0becef7) message; the resourcesearch guide mentions the enqueue but not the lag

because.text: No document a test author reads states that search results lag writes; the CT helper polls, but only its code shows it
The authoring loop has a rule for counts but none for views a background job builds
because.evidence: flow-suite-testing SKILL.md before this change: no mention of polling or projections

because.text: The flow-suite-testing skill did not say that a read of a projection waits through a poll
The racy definition reached the CI-tagged flow in both orgs, and five of six repeat runs passed
because.evidence: CI-org runs at 11:12:18Z-11:12:23Z and dev-org runs at 11:14:13Z-11:14:15Z were green

because.text: Authoring runs hit an idle dev API, where the sync worker usually beats a request that leaves 50 ms after create
because.evidence: `sync_service.go` comment: bursts of sync jobs once starved fresh resources out of search for tens of seconds

because.text: The repeat-run gate samples an idle API; a CI burst slows the worker, so the gate under-samples the race the suite will meet

contributing: The generator updates the tagged flow in place, so the new definition is in the suite as soon as it is saved.

Building the poll took two more tries: a `poll` body sees only flow inputs, a `{{$runId}}` in a module binding resolves in the child, and JSONPath does not descend into a final output. None of this was written down.

well: The three-run gate in a second org caught the race before any CI run used the definition.
The sibling searches in the failing run found the spec, which pointed at timing rather than at the search query within minutes.
wrong: The commit message of the feature under test was trusted over its code; the enqueue was in plain view in `search_sync.go`.
The first two poll modules were written without reading how a `poll` body gets its inputs.
lucky: The race showed in the sixth run. On an idle API it could have passed all six and first failed in CI under a burst, where it reads as a regression of #508.
No other flow in the suites asserts on search right after a write; `echopoint: catalog and org` only checks that the flows domain is non-empty.

actions.what: `echopoint: specs` polls through `specs: search poll (module)` before searching, in both orgs
flow-suite-testing skill: a read of a projection polls; how a poll module gets this run's values
resourcesearch AGENTS.md: documents follow a write through the queue; tests poll
searchResources description in openapi.yaml states that results follow a write after a short delay
Poll budget 30 s (60 attempts at 500 ms) so a CI burst does not exhaust it
After changing a CI-tagged flow, the routine reruns its whole tag in both orgs before the run ends, so the change meets the suite's own load

messaging.internal: SEV4 flow flake: `echopoint: specs` searched a new spec before the queued search indexing job wrote it. Flow now polls until the spec is searchable; skill and resourcesearch guide updated. No CI run affected.
